title: Renewal Signal Deep Dive & Exit Plan (working draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working deep-dive template to investigate emergent renewal risk signals, synthesize root causes, and propose a short list of tailored mitigation and exit plays for executive escalation. Designed to be used by CS AEs + AMs during the 6-12 week pre-renewal window and updated live during QBR prep.

How to use this doc (quick runbook)
- Stage 0: Triage (day 0): Pull basic telemetry, recent support activity, ARR trend, contract terms. Quick yes/no on near-term churn risk.
- Stage 1: Signal consolidation (day 1–3): Gather evidence across product usage, NPS/CSAT, billing disputes, executive engagement, and roadmap alignment. Populate the scorecard below.
- Stage 2: Root-cause hypothesis (day 3–7): Interview stakeholders, review tickets, and classify causes (value, adoption, product fit, commercial, org change).
- Stage 3: Tailored response (day 7–14): Design 2–3 mitigation plays ranked by expected impact and effort. Map stakeholders and timelines.
- Stage 4: Exec escalation (as needed): If risk >= 7/10 or time-to-renew < 30 days and mitigation high-effort, run the exec escalation briefing. Use the one-pager in the Exec folder.

SECTION A — Quick scorecard (fill during Triage)
- Customer name: [customer] 
- ARR ($): [ARR] 
- Contract renewal date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Renewal window status: [>90d, 60–90d, 30–60d, <30d]
- Primary indicator(s) triggering this doc: [drop in MAU, exec churn, legal T&Cs, pricing pressure, support spike, adoption plateau]
- Risk score (1–10): [numeric]
- Confidence (low/med/high): [text]
- Recommended immediate next step: [call, QBR refresh, legal review, discount proposal]

SECTION B — Evidence matrix (paste links / snippets)
- Product engagement (last 90d): daily active users, sessions per seat, key flows completed — summary line and 2 supporting metrics or links to dashboards.
- Support volume & severity (last 90d): ticket count, P1/P2 incidents, outstanding bugs impacting deliverables.
- Financial signals: invoices disputed, payments delayed, reduction in seat counts, usage drop.
- Executive contact: C-level / VP reachouts last 180d (dates + topics).
- Roadmap alignment: features requested vs. committed; blockers on delivery.
- Competitive intel: disclosed alternatives, PoC with competitor, price comparisons.
- Legal/compliance snags: contract addenda, SSO/KMS requirements, data residency issues.
- Voice of customer: recent CSAT/NPS snippets, quoted language that signals dissatisfaction.

SECTION C — Root-cause hypothesis (pick all that apply, add short evidence)
- Value gap: customer not getting measurable ROI; missing key metric. [evidence]
- Adoption friction: onboarding incomplete, platform UX edge-case, missing integrations. [evidence]
- Reliability/regression: performance regressions, incidents undermining trust. [evidence]
- Commercial misalignment: pricing packaging misfit, renewal expectations not managed. [evidence]
- Org change: sponsor left, reorg deprioritized use case. [evidence]
- Competitive displacement attempt: vendor outreach, aggressive feature parity. [evidence]
- Legal/regulatory constraint: new compliance mandate blocking progress. [evidence]

SECTION D — Mitigation & save plays (template entries; pick 1 primary + 1 backup)
Each play should include: objective, timeline, required owners, success criteria, blocker list, cost/discount impact, PR approval required (yes/no).

Play 1: Tactical Adoption Sprint (low cost, medium impact)
- Objective: Recover 20–30% of active seats and re-establish core workflows within 6 weeks.
- Timeline: 6-week sprint: week 0 (coaching plan), weeks 1–3 (targeted enablement), weeks 4–6 (adoption measurement + small product fixes).
- Owners: CS Owner (Aisha), Solutions Engineer (Marco), Customer Success Manager (owner-assigned), Product PM (named).
- Success criteria: X% MAU recovery, 3 feature adoption milestones completed, CSAT >= 4.0 in follow-up survey.
- Blockers: backlog priority, SE availability, customer project schedule.
- Cost: $0–$25k in professional services; no contract amendment.
- PR approval required: no.

Play 2: Accelerated Delivery + Commit (higher cost, high impact)
- Objective: Commit to delivery of 2 high-priority roadmap items within contract window to preserve strategic value.
- Timeline: 8–12 weeks with a delivery SOW.
- Owners: Product (PM), Eng leads, Solutions Eng, CS Exec sponsor, Sales.
- Success criteria: feature shipped to staging, acceptance test passed, exec-level sign-off.
- Blockers: engineering capacity, conflicting roadmap priorities.
- Cost: SOW estimate + potential revenue deferral; requires cross-functional approval.
- PR approval required: yes (Product + Engineering leadership).

Play 3: Commercial Restructure (pricing concession with guardrails)
- Objective: Offer a limited-term pricing concession tied to usage growth and renewal commitment.
- Timeline: immediate offer; 30–90 day review.
- Owners: Account Exec, Sales Ops, Legal, CS Director.
- Success criteria: signed amendment, payment terms honored, usage growth >= X% by review date.
- Blockers: discount lobbying precedent, procurement approval, legal terms.
- Cost: modeled concession ($ / seat or % off) — attach finance worksheet.
- PR approval required: yes (Sales leadership + Finance).

Play 4: Executive Sponsor Intervention (fast escalation)
- Objective: Re-engage C-suite or sponsoring execs to revalidate strategic alignment.
- Timeline: 2 weeks to secure meeting, 1–2 follow-ups.
- Owners: CS Exec (VP level), Customer Exec sponsor, Account Exec.
- Success criteria: exec alignment on roadmap or a written renewal commitment.
- Blockers: sponsor availability, competing priorities.
- Cost: negligible but high sensitivity.
- PR approval required: no (but prep with Legal for any commitments).

SECTION E — Decision matrix (quick choose)
- If risk >=8 and <30 days to renew -> prioritize Play 3 + Play 4 (commercial + exec).
- If risk 5–7 and adoption gap present -> prioritize Play 1 + Play 2.
- If reliability incident was cause -> immediate engineering hotfix + Play 4.
- If legal/compliance -> escalate to Legal + Private Deploy team; freeze commercial concessions until compliance is cleared.

SECTION F — Communication templates (quick copy/paste)
1) Exec re-engagement email (subject): "Quick alignment on [customer]’s roadmap & renewal"
Hi [Exec Name],
We’d like 20 minutes to align on progress against [outcome], share a short remediation plan we’re executing, and confirm priorities ahead of your renewal on [renewal date]. Proposed times: [2 options].
Best,
[Aisha]

2) Internal escalation note (Slack)
- TL;DR: [Customer] risk 8/10. Root cause: adoption + missed roadmap commitments. Asking for: Product sprint for feature X (2 weeks) + Exec meeting.
- Links: [scorecard], [tickets], [dashboard]

SECTION G — Timeline & owners (populate with calendar dates)
- Day 0–3: scorecard + initial customer touchpoint (CSM)
- Day 4–10: stakeholder interviews + build mitigation plan
- Day 10–21: execute primary play (enablement / SOW / discount offering)
- Day 21–45: measure impact; if not trending, escalate to exec step and Sales leadership

SECTION H — Approval & handoffs
- If play requires >$25k PS or any pricing concession >10% -> notify Sales Ops + Finance (must sign off).
- If legal term changes -> Ops Legal review required before customer-facing docs.
- Product commitments that alter roadmap > 2 sprints -> Eng + Product leadership approval and updated roadmap published to CORES.

Open questions / Known unknowns
- Has procurement raised specific T&Cs that block shipment? (ask Sales Ops)
- Is there a hard dependency on an integration that’s backlog-blocked? (ask Platform/Integrations)
- Who is the true economic buyer now after the 2/2025 reorg? (confirm via exec outreach)

Appendix — quick checklists
- Pre-QBR prep checklist: updated scorecard, 2–3 wins since last QBR, rolling backlog status, list of outstanding commitments with ETA.
- Evidence capture checklist: links to dashboards, ticket IDs, payment issues with dates, copy of last two executive emails.
- Post-save retrospective: what worked, what didn’t, costs incurred, long-term guardrails to avoid repeat.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep this file lean: pull in granular data via links rather than bloating this doc.
- For any approved concessions, capture an internal one-pager with decision rationale for future renewals — minimize precedent risk.

Version history (brief)
- 2025-02-18 v0.1 — initial draft for CS squad review (Aisha)
- 2025-02-25 v0.2 — added commercial play templates and finance thresholds (Connor)
- 2025-03-01 v0.3 — inserted evidence matrix and exec email templates (Priya)

End of working draft
